content.goal: Enable a vibration-monitoring device that attaches to a machine, records vibration data, and supports detecting meaningful changes in how the machine is operating while confirming vibration bandwidth, dynamic range, recording mode, and mounting/baseline constraints before component selection.
content.problemStatement: The initial vibration-monitoring device concept requires a functional architecture, but key measurement bandwidth, dynamic range, recording-mode/session constraints, and mounting/baseline calibration needs remain unconfirmed. The prototype must remain non-component-specific until these unknowns are resolved.
content.intendedContext: An early-stage team will prototype the device, attach it to a machine, collect vibration recordings, and export analysis-ready logs to validate change-detection assumptions and next embedded steps.
scope: Functional specification for vibration sensing and timestamped data storage.
Functional design for buffering/recording and providing analysis-ready change-detection inputs.
Explicit identification of unknown bandwidth, dynamic range, recording mode, and mounting/baseline constraints.
outOfScope: Component-part selection (specific sensors, ADCs, MCUs, storage devices).
Firmware generation, PCB layout, schematic validation, and simulation execution.
Production manufacturing planning and deployment infrastructure.
successCriteria: All produced artifacts conform to the v1 contracts.
Explicit and inferred requirements are distinguishable.
Unsupported assumptions are not presented as facts.
The Next Action is derived from concrete blockers and open questions about vibration measurement needs.

assumptions.statement: Initial prototypes can capture vibration as analysis-ready logs while calibration and mounting unknowns are still open, as long as assumptions are surfaced explicitly as open questions.
